purpose: Facts added or corrected after the Level-2 record was fixed. The Level-2 files are unchanged; scripts that use these facts read them from here.

regime_corrections.reason: The regime rule gives `both` to an item whose repetitions include smooth-wall and rough-wall flows. This case is one flow over a wall of alternating rough and smooth strips (sand-grain roughness of 130 wall units on the rough strip in every run), so no repetition is a smooth-wall flow. A heterogeneous rough wall is `rough` under the rule.

quote.text: heterogeneous roughness configuration consists of alternating rough and smooth strips oriented perpendicular to the mean flow direction.

regime_corrections.effect: The contrast leaves the primary-scope basis of the outcome counts (117 to 116 member contrasts). No work-level count of Level 2 changes: N437-K02, a smooth-wall channel, is a strict member within the primary scope.
regime_corrections.raised_by: panel review of the Level-2 record

qualified_transfer_tests.question: Does the target of each qualified transfer test lie inside the ranges that the source states for the fitting set, in a flow of the fitting set?

values.within stated ranges: a flow of the fitting set at parameter values inside every stated range
values.beyond a stated range: at least one stated parameter range of the fitting set is exceeded
values.another flow: a flow or geometry that is not in the fitting set, at parameter values that exceed no stated range
values.fitting set not described: the source does not describe the fitting set

P19-T06.basis: Channel at Re_tau = 700 with sudden spanwise pressure gradient, Pi = 80; stated training ranges Re_tau = 100-1000 and Pi = 5-100 (transfer_exposure.json, target)

P19-T01.basis: Laminar flat-plate boundary layer; the laminar building block is Poiseuille flow

P19-T02.basis: Zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer; the building block is the turbulent channel; Reynolds number and resolution lie among the training values

P19-T03.basis: Turbulent pipe at Re_tau of about 40,000; training channels reach Re_tau = 10,000

P19-T04.basis: Poiseuille-Couette flow; three values of Re_P lie beyond the stated training range

P19-T05.basis: Poiseuille-Couette flow; four values of Re_P lie beyond the stated training range

N497-T02.basis: Channel at Re_tau = 2000; the channel training data are at Re_tau = 1000

P01-T01.basis: Backward-facing step; the coefficients were fitted by other authors to pipe, plane-duct and Couette profiles

N037-T01.basis: The source gives the roughness correlation and its reference only

condition_factors.question: For each contrast whose order changes between conditions: which single factor separates two conditions that give opposite orders for one class of quantity?
condition_factors.coding: Coded once by the author of the scripts from the condition descriptions recorded in contrast_outcomes.json. Not read twice. Each entry names two conditions that differ in the named factor alone and that code/derive_outcomes.py finds to give opposite orders. A contrast with no such pair is 'several together'.

values.grid: grid spacing or first-cell height, at the same Reynolds number and numerics
values.numerical scheme: convection scheme, on the same grid with the same closure
values.outer closure: subgrid-scale or Reynolds-averaged turbulence closure, on the same grid and scheme
values.Reynolds number: Reynolds number on the same grid
values.another flow parameter: rotation number, Mach number, forcing frequency or angle of attack
values.sampling height: height at which the wall law samples the flow, where the contrast changes something else
values.another part of the method: a component of the near-wall method other than the one the contrast changes
values.several together: every pair of conditions with opposite orders differs in more than one factor

N181-K02.note: formulation of the wall-modelled boundary condition

N262-K01.note: bulk Mach number 0.8 against 1.5 at Re_b = 17,000

N297-K04.note: the wall law with which the sampling arrangements are compared

N358-K03.note: interface condition on turbulent kinetic energy
